A lightweight, privacy-first image editor that runs entirely in the browser with WASM.

Pixel Forge lets users crop, resize, and apply filters to images without uploading anything — all processing happens client-side via Rust compiled to WebAssembly.

## Why WASM?

Image transforms run 4–6× faster than the equivalent JavaScript canvas pipeline, and the UI stays responsive by offloading work to Web Workers.

A Practical Guide to Web Performance Budgets
Setting and enforcing performance budgets so your site stays fast as it grows.

Performance is a feature that silently degrades. Budgets make regressions visible.

## Start with metrics

Track LCP, INP, and CLS at the 75th percentile of real users, not lab data.

## Enforce in CI

Fail the build when bundle size or Lighthouse scores regress. A budget nobody enforces is a wish.

How we cut lead time from days to hours by moving to trunk-based development and feature flags.

Long-lived feature branches create merge pain and slow feedback loops. Here's how our team switched to trunk-based development.

## The problem

We averaged 3-day lead time from PR to production, mostly spent waiting on reviews and resolving merge conflicts.

## What changed

1. Branches live less than a day
2. Every feature ships behind a flag
3. Small PRs get reviewed within the hour

## Results

Lead time dropped to under 4 hours, and rollback became trivial — flip the flag off.
